entities.summary: Diogo de Azambuja (1432–1518) was a Portuguese noble and explorer who played a crucial role in the Age of Discovery. He was born in the kingdom of Portugal, which was then a major power in Europe. In 1460, he joined the Portuguese royal court, where he served as a page and later became a page in the royal household. During this time, he met Prince Henry the Navigator, who would become his mentor and patron. Azambuja accompanied Henry on several expeditions to West Africa and the Atlantic Islands, including the Azores and the Canary Islands. He was also involved in the establishment of the Portuguese East India Company, which would go on to become a major player in the global spice trade. Azambuja's adventures took him to the coast of West Africa, where he encountered the Portuguese explorer João Fernandes, who would later become the first European to reach the Cape of Good Hope. Azambuja's travels also took him to the island of Madagascar, where he encountered the Malagasy people and established trade relations with them. Despite his many accomplishments, Azambuja's life was marked by tragedy, including the loss of his daughter and his own death in 1518. He was buried in the cathedral of Lisbon, where many other Portuguese nobles were also interred. Azambuja's legacy lived on, however, as he was remembered as a hero by the Portuguese people and a symbol of their national identity. His name became synonymous with bravery and exploration, and he was celebrated in poetry and song throughout the centuries. Today, Azambuja is remembered as one of the most important figures in Portuguese history, and his name is still celebrated in Lisbon and other parts of Portugal.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Azambuja's travels took him to the coast of West Africa, where he encountered the Portuguese explorer João Fernandes, who would later become the first European to reach the Cape of Good Hope. His adventures also took him to the island of Madagascar, where he encountered the Malagasy people and established trade relations with them.
